absent: Numeric values and limits for staging length, location code length, minor start, default and maximum adapter counts, and termios contents.
Signatures and behavior of hypervisor character transfer, partner info query and free, connection register and free, and virtual interrupt enable and disable helpers.
Definitions of the global adapter list head, rescan status flag, kicked flag, index table storage, driver name and node strings, tty driver pointer, operations tables, and attribute group objects.
Open, close, write, write room, hangup, and other tty operation handlers and port reference counting rules beyond destruct.
Probe versus remove versus open races, module load and unload teardown, and full initialization failure unwind beyond the shown fragment.
Format details of partner information entries and firmware error code meanings beyond busy and invalid argument handling.

findings.text: Per server adapter record embeds a tty port and a private spinlock, then a numeric tty complement index, an integer work bitmap, a fixed size output staging area with a staged byte count, a connected flag, partner unit address and partner partition identifiers, a partner location string sized one beyond the location code limit for termination, a list linkage, a virtual device pointer, and an optional destruction completion pointer. Fields from the connected flag onward stay valid without an attached tty and are released only when object references drop.

Work bitmap reserves the lowest bit for scheduled read with value one, the next bit for quick read with value two, and the next bit for attempted write with value four. A combined read mask covers the two read bits.

Each adapter record lock guards its bitmap, connection flag, partner identifiers, location string, index, staged output state, and device linkage. Attribute views, state changes, throttle controls, interrupt handling, and IO progress hold it, normally preserving interrupt state, while the interrupt entry uses the plain form suited to interrupt context.

A global spinlock guards the list linking all adapter records. Rescan, worker iteration, probe insertion, and port destruction acquire it outermost and may then take one record lock at a time. No reverse nesting is shown.

A dedicated global spinlock guards the single shared partner information staging page and its null check. Refresh validates the pointer and performs the firmware query under this lock, then releases it before updating the adapter record and freeing temporary entries.

A global mutex serializes one time core setup so concurrent probes either observe completion or perform it once. It covers tty driver allocation, index table creation, driver registration, staging page allocation, and worker thread creation, with ordered unwind on each failure path.

Device indexes come from a table sized during initialization where negative one means free. Allocation scans upward for the lowest free slot and marks it used, returning failure when full. Release validates range and table presence and restores negative one. The table starts fully free and is cleared on teardown.

Partner identity counts as present only when both unit address and partition identifier are nonzero. Refresh first clears both to zero so a departed partner leaves no stale identity, then applies each discovered entry by copying address, partition, and location text including termination, and finally releases the temporary list. Missing staging storage fails without modifying the record.

Writing terminal state accepts only numeric zero; any nonzero numeric value is rejected as invalid. The request is then denied when the port still has users or when the server is already disconnected. Otherwise the live connection is torn down under the record lock and the supplied byte count is reported as consumed.

Changing the current virtual terminal through sysfs is always refused for permission reasons. The five device attributes expose partner address, partner location, current terminal, connection state, and index respectively, each read under the record lock and rendered as one line, with address in uppercase hexadecimal and state and index in decimal.

A driver level rescan attribute reports whether refresh is in progress. A store requesting refresh marks busy, walks every adapter refreshing partner data, then marks idle and reports consumed length. A store that does not request refresh while busy is rejected.

A single worker thread loops clearing a kicked flag with ordering, then walks all adapters invoking per adapter progress and accumulating pending work. When write retry or quick read remains it yields and immediately repeats; otherwise it sleeps interruptibly until kicked. It terminates only when asked to stop.

Per adapter progress first attempts pending output, then abandons input when no tty is bound, when the tty is throttled, or when no read bit is set, clearing read bits in the unbound or throttled case. Otherwise it clears read bits, fetches up to one staging length of input when sufficient flip room exists, queues it with normal marking, requests quick follow up when any byte arrived, pushes outside the lock, and reenables device interrupts only when nothing arrived.

Buffered output is offered only while the write retry bit is set and only as a whole; partial delivery is not accepted. A positive transfer count clears the staged count and the retry bit and wakes an attached tty. Zero or negative outcome leaves staged state and bitmap unchanged, and delivery remains owed even when the tty has gone away.

Receive flow control has three entries. The interrupt entry suspends device interrupts, sets scheduled read, and wakes the worker. The unthrottle entry sets scheduled read under the record lock and wakes the worker. The throttle entry only suspends device interrupts under the record lock.

Probe validates parameters, ensures core initialization, claims an index early to simplify cleanup, allocates and zeroes a record, initializes its port and lock, links record and virtual device in both directions, fetches initial partner data with failure only logged, and appends the record to the global list without enabling interrupts because no reader exists yet.

Removal records an on stack completion, takes a tty reference under the record lock, hangs up and releases that tty when present, drops the port reference, and waits for destruction. Destruction unlinks the record under global and record locks, tears down any live connection, clears device linkage and partner identity, returns the index, zeroes the location string, frees the record, and signals completion.

Connection setup first attempts registration with cached partner identity and marks connected on success. On invalid argument it refreshes partner data, fails when refresh fails or no partner remains, retries once, and treats a second invalid argument as busy. Other first attempt failures propagate directly without retry.

Connection release repeats while the firmware reports busy and only then marks disconnected, so callers must allow unbounded retries. Device enable that fails after requesting an interrupt line must release that line and free the partner connection under the record lock before reporting failure.

The virtual IO driver binds probe, remove, name, and device and driver attribute groups, and matches the serial server compatible pair shown in its identifier table. Core initialization chooses a tty count from a module parameter clamped to a supported range, allocates a raw mode tty driver with a fixed minor start and custom no echo termios, registers it, allocates one staging page, and starts the single worker thread.
Flip insertion helpers always tag newly received bytes with the normal marking and forward them to the underlying flagged insertion primitive.

Rescan and the worker iterate the global adapter list while holding its lock and acquire each record lock in turn; sleeping or acquiring the global lock from inside a record lock would deadlock or violate atomic context. The shared staging page must never be dereferenced without holding its dedicated lock and checking for null.
